# Eavesy

> Eavesy is a free, open-source (Apache-2.0) Mac app for Apple silicon (macOS 13+) that keeps what you say, hear, see and copy as plain files on your disk, as Markdown your AI agent can read. It works without an account. Signing in at eavesy.com adds cloud transcripts, briefs, search, chat and MCP access. Source: https://github.com/williamrogersdev/eavesy

Everyone gets the same fair-use limits: https://eavesy.com/docs/fair-use-limits

## Capture modes (Mac app)
- Talk (default shortcut Cmd+Shift+D, can be set to fn): microphone only. Tap toggles, hold longer than 350 ms for push-to-talk. Pastes on-device text where the cursor is, with or without an account. Any cleanup happens only in the cloud copy. Docs: https://eavesy.com/docs/talk-and-dictation
- Meeting: microphone plus the audio the Mac plays. No screen. No bot joins the call. Docs: https://eavesy.com/docs/meetings
- Video: screen, its audio, and the microphone. Docs: https://eavesy.com/docs/video
- Screenshot: pick an area (macOS 14+). Clipboard (Cmd+V in the launcher), quick notes, and dropped files are kept too. Signed in, notes, clipboard text, screenshots and pasted images also upload to the account and sync to the user's other Macs; signed out, they stay on the Mac. Docs: https://eavesy.com/docs/screenshots-and-notes

Open Eavesy: Cmd+Shift+Space. Only Open and Talk are global shortcuts. Docs: https://eavesy.com/docs/keyboard-shortcuts

## Transcripts
- On-device live captions while recording (on by default). The cloud transcript (Whisper on Cloudflare Workers AI, signed in only) replaces them.
- Meetings are labelled You and Them by track. There is no per-person diarization.
- Spoken language defaults to English; automatic detection or another language is under Settings > Transcription > Spoken language in the web app. Up to 100 custom words under Settings > Transcription.
- Briefs: title, summary, decisions, action items, open questions. Built-in formats and custom templates can regenerate them.

## Web app
Browser recorder (account required; uploads in about 4-minute segments), a capture bar for audio, webcam or screen video and screenshots (uploaded), and drops between your signed-in browsers. Browser recordings are copied to a signed-in Mac's ~/Eavesy/Recordings without audio. Docs: https://eavesy.com/docs/browser-recorder

There is no iPhone, iPad, Windows, Linux or Intel Mac app.

## Where the files live
The Mac app writes each capture to a folder under `~/Eavesy/Recordings/` (change it under Settings > Recordings folder in the Mac app). Folders are named `<YYYY-MM-DD> <title at start>`, for example `2026-06-15 Meeting recording`, and are never renamed. A clash gets ` (HH-MM)` added. Launcher screenshots use `Screenshot-<id>`.

```text
~/Eavesy/Recordings/2026-06-15 Meeting recording/
├── summary.md       # brief
├── transcript.md    # on-device text, then the cloud transcript
├── notes.md         # the user's own notes
├── meeting.json     # schemaVersion, id, remoteMeetingId, title, date, startedAt, durationSeconds, source, status, files
├── audio.m4a
└── screen.mp4       # Video mode only
```

Clipboard, screenshot and imported captures hold `note.md`, `image.png` or `screenshot.png` plus `capture.json`. Format: https://eavesy.com/docs/session-folder-format

## Connect over MCP
Server: `https://mcp.eavesy.com` (streamable HTTP). Add it by URL: the server supports MCP authorization (OAuth 2.1, PKCE, dynamic client registration, metadata at `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`), so clients like Claude.ai, ChatGPT and Claude Code send the user to sign in to Eavesy and approve the connection. No token to paste.

Claude Code:

```bash
claude mcp add --scope user --transport http eavesy https://mcp.eavesy.com
```

Or the Claude Code plugin (adds the server plus a skill for when to use it): `/plugin marketplace add williamrogersdev/eavesy`, then `/plugin install eavesy@eavesy`.

Scopes: `read` (default) and `write`. The user grants write only by ticking "Also let it write" on the approval page (or "Allow writes" for a pasted token). Tools a connection's scopes don't cover are hidden from `tools/list` and refused if called.

Fallback for clients without OAuth: create a connection in the web app under Settings > AI assistants (MCP); the token is shown once. Send it in the Authorization header. Tokens expire 90 days after last use. URL-path tokens (`https://mcp.eavesy.com/<token>`) are deprecated and work only while the server flag `MCP_ALLOW_PATH_TOKENS` is not `false`.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "eavesy": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://mcp.eavesy.com",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" }
    }
  }
}
```

Library tools, all read-only. Start with `search` or `recent`, then `get`:
- `search` (query, kinds, project, since, until, limit): everything in the account library: recordings, dictations, notes, screenshots, images, video and audio captures. Word matches across all, plus matches by meaning for recordings and dictations (counts against the daily search quota). Returns {items: [{id, kind, title, excerpt, project, created_at, duration_sec, url, score}]} as text and structuredContent.
- `recent` (kinds, project, since, until, limit): newest items, same filters and shape. kinds: meeting, dictation, note, image, video, audio. Dates are ISO 8601 (UTC unless an offset is given; a bare `until` date covers the whole day).
- `get` (id, transcript_format: agent|raw): one item. A recording with summary, the user's notes and transcript; a dictation's text; a note's Markdown; a screenshot or image with any text read from it plus the image as MCP image content (up to 4 MB).

Older recording-only tools (names say "meeting" because that is the recording type in the data model):
- `search_library` (query): retrieve source evidence from completed synced account recordings.
- `ask_library` (question): answer from recording evidence when cloud answers are enabled; may abstain or report unanswered parts and context limits. Each call counts against the user's daily AI answer quota.
- `list_projects`: list projects available to the connection.
- `search_meetings` (query, limit): search recordings by title or transcript; returns excerpts.
- `get_meeting` (id): summary, the user's notes and full transcript.
- `recent_meetings` (limit): newest recordings.
- `search_dictations` (query, limit): search dictations.
- `get_action_items` (status: open|completed|all, owner): action items across recordings.
- `get_account_info`: which account and connection this is, its access and expiry.

Tools that are not read-only:
- `send_to_human` (text, spoken): show a message on the user's Mac and read a short version aloud.
- `ask_human` (question, spoken, choices, timeout_sec): ask the user on their Mac and wait for the typed answer.
- `sign_out`: disconnect this connection (only when the user asks).

Only what is in the account is available over MCP: recordings, dictations, web captures, and notes, clipboard text, screenshots and images from a Mac that was signed in. Mac screenshots match by title only (no text is read from them), but `get` returns the image. Anything else is on disk under ~/Eavesy/Recordings. Docs: https://eavesy.com/docs/connect-mcp

## Copy-paste examples
Paste into an agent after copying a brief from Eavesy:

```text
Here is the context from my call (Markdown below). Draft the follow-up tasks as a checklist.
<paste summary.md>
```

Ask an MCP-connected agent:

```text
Use Eavesy to find the recording where we discussed the pricing change, then list the open action items.
```

Point a coding agent at the folder:

```bash
grep -ril "pricing" ~/Eavesy/Recordings/*/transcript.md
```

## Bring your own keys
In the web app under Settings > AI providers you can connect your own OpenRouter account or add an Anthropic API key. Keys are entered on the web and stored encrypted. The Mac app keeps only its device token in the Keychain.

## Self-hosting
Eavesy runs on Cloudflare (Workers, D1, R2, KV, Queues, Vectorize, Workers AI) with Clerk for sign-in. Guide: https://github.com/williamrogersdev/eavesy/blob/main/docs/SELF_HOSTING.md

## Practical resources

- Guides: https://eavesy.com/guides

- Cursor handoff: https://eavesy.com/integrations/cursor
- Local file and attachment boundaries: https://eavesy.com/guides/share-local-recordings-with-ai

Mac version 0.5.4 does not automatically extract a visual frame timeline or provide the newer local walkthrough MCP server. Audio transcripts establish spoken words; an agent needs actual image or video access to inspect visual details. A path pasted into a browser chat does not upload the file. Hosted MCP reaches notes, clipboard text, screenshots and images only once they have synced from a signed-in Mac.

The worked examples are explicitly fictional teaching material, with hand-authored sample text. They are not customer recordings, production model responses, or claims that Eavesy automatically generated a visual report. Their fixture screenshot depicts the included demo.
